chunks: And it is narrated from Ibn Muskan, from Ishaq al-Mada'ini, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group of God be upon him) about a group of people who board a ship to purchase food, negotiate its price, and then one of them buys it. The others ask him for it, and he gives them what they want of the food, while the owner of the food is the one who delivers it to them and receives the payment. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in this; I do not see it other than that they have shared in it.' I said: 'Indeed, the owner of the food calls a measurer to measure it for us, and we have laborers who check it, so it increases and decreases.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in it, as long as it is not a significant error.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on one person buying food for a group and distributing it with potential measurement variations?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the practice of group purchasing on ships, interpreting the transaction as a form of shared ownership (sharikah) where the buyer acts as an agent for the collective. He permits minor discrepancies in measurement by hired laborers, establishing a legal principle that insignificant errors (ghalat) do not invalidate the sale, thereby facilitating trade in communal settings.
